LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 9.3.1 WORD SETS (GENDER SETS FOR ANIMALS/PEOPLE) OPPOSITES

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.3: Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to learn words for referring to male and female animals/ people?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the gender sets of animals and people in a conversation,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use the opposites to discuss animals and people at the farm,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. realise the role of gender sets and opposites in communicating ideas.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the gender sets of animals and people in a conversation,

   Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use the opposites to discuss animals and people at the farm,

   Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. realise the role of gender sets and opposites in communicating ideas.

   Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss with peers the names of males and females of domestic animals.

2. discuss with peers the difference between male and female,

3. construct sentences using male and female of animals that are familiar.

4. work with pictures or picture descriptions to identify opposites of animals /people.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss with peers the names of males and females of domestic animals.
2. discuss with peers the difference between male and female,
3. construct sentences using male and female of animals that are familiar.
4. work with pictures or picture descriptions to identify opposites of animals /people.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language use 9.3.1 Word Sets (gender sets for animals/people) Opposites together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration; the learner’s writing skills are enhanced as they write sentences correctly using gender sets.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as the learner appreciates diverse opinions from peers during discussions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self-esteem); the learner’s esteem is nurtured as they as the learner identifies gender sets of animals and people.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Gender sets are learnt in Kiswahili and Indigenous Language Activities.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the gender sets of animals and people in a conversation,
2. use the opposites to discuss animals and people at the farm,
3. realise the role of gender sets and opposites in communicating ideas.

Remember the key question: Why is it important to learn words for referring to male and female animals/ people?
